title: std.time.nanoTimestamp missing on x86_64-macos target (2 call sites)
registered_by: Found while fixing ISS-0134 (Linux Environ portability); verified via cross-compile
scope: macOS cross-compilation only. No impact on Linux CI or Windows development.
symptom: zig build -Dtarget=x86_64-macos fails with 2 errors: std.time.nanoTimestamp has no member on this target, in src/admin/tenant_migration.zig:685 and src/api/routes/onboarding.zig:24. Both are @intCast(std.time.nanoTimestamp()) in the non-Windows fallback branch of a PRNG seed helper. Confirmed this is macOS-specific, not a general POSIX gap: -Dtarget=x86_64-linux-gnu and -Dtarget=aarch64-linux-gnu both compile the identical lines cleanly.
root_cause_analysis: Not yet investigated in depth -- found incidentally while cross-compile-verifying the ISS-0134 fix across x86_64-linux-gnu, aarch64-linux-gnu, and x86_64-macos. Filed separately rather than folded into ISS-0134 since it is a distinct stdlib API gap unrelated to Environ.
acceptance_criteria: zig build -Dtarget=aarch64-macos exits 0 (not yet checked either way)
